definition: The trained habit of doing the hard thing. He sets it equal to freedom.
example: Discipline equals freedom.

definition: Room to act. He says discipline is the pathway to it, not the opposite of it.
example: But, in fact, discipline is the pathway to freedom.

definition: To allow something to continue. He says a leader's real standard is what they tolerate, not what they preach.
example: It's not what you preach, it's what you tolerate.

definition: Taking the result as yours. For him it covers the mistakes, the failures, and the plan to win.
example: The leader must acknowledge mistakes and admit failures, take ownership of them, and develop a plan to win.

definition: To admit openly. The first move of ownership is to acknowledge the mistake.
example: The leader must acknowledge mistakes and admit failures, take ownership of them, and develop a plan to win.

definition: The duty for an outcome. He places both success and failure on the leader.
example: On any team, in any organization, all responsibility for success and failure rests with the leader.

definition: A route toward something. Discipline, he says, is the pathway to freedom.
example: But, in fact, discipline is the pathway to freedom.

definition: Self-importance that, in his account, clouds planning and blocks good advice.
example: Ego clouds and disrupts everything: the planning process, the ability to take good advice, and the ability to accept constructive criticism.

definition: To throw into disorder. Ego, he says, does this to plans, advice, and criticism.
example: Ego clouds and disrupts everything: the planning process, the ability to take good advice, and the ability to accept constructive criticism.

definition: Judgment of your work. He says ego blocks the constructive kind.
example: Ego clouds and disrupts everything: the planning process, the ability to take good advice, and the ability to accept constructive criticism.

definition: Meant to build or improve. The criticism a leader has to be able to take.
example: Ego clouds and disrupts everything: the planning process, the ability to take good advice, and the ability to accept constructive criticism.

definition: Below the level that was set. If it is accepted, he says, it becomes the new standard.
example: If substandard performance is accepted and no one is held accountable, that poor performance becomes the new standard.

definition: Required to answer for a result. Without that, he says, a poor performance resets the standard.
example: If substandard performance is accepted and no one is held accountable, that poor performance becomes the new standard.

definition: What follows from an action. He says that with none, the poor performance becomes the rule.
example: If substandard performance is accepted and no one is held accountable — if there are no consequences — that poor performance becomes the new standard.

definition: The level that is actually enforced. Tolerated failure, he says, writes a new one.
example: That poor performance becomes the new standard. Therefore, leaders must enforce standards.

definition: A failure of resolve. He locates the day's first one in staying in bed after the alarm.
example: If you are mentally weak for that moment and you let that weakness keep you in bed, you fail.

definition: To move with intent. Disciplined procedures, he writes, increased the team's freedom to maneuver.
example: Our freedom to operate and maneuver had increased substantially through disciplined procedures.

definition: By a large amount. His measure of how much disciplined procedure increased freedom to maneuver.
example: Our freedom to operate and maneuver had increased substantially through disciplined procedures.

definition: A reversal. On the podcast he takes the setback and turns it into something useful.
example: Take that issue, take that setback, take that problem, and turn it into something good.

definition: To set your aim again after a hit. The step in his close, between reloading and re-engaging.
example: So get up, dust off, reload, recalibrate, re-engage — and go out on the attack.
